Mr. Speaker, during the recess of parliament, my colleagues and I from northern Ontario travelled rather extensively throughout that vast region which extends from the Manitoba boundary to the boundary of Quebec. Incidentally, that huge region of which I speak is much more than the hinterland of Toronto. It is also something greater than the underdeveloped backyard of Ontario. Northern Ontario in itself is, and must continue to be considered by the federal government as one of the major economic and geographic regions of this country. During our tour, my fellow members of parliament and myself sensed a new attitude of optimism among the people who inhabit this region. Far from feeling neglected and forgotten, these citizens of Canada now see that the future is on their side and that greater prosperity and economic development is on the verge of being theirs.
